issues.legal_issue: A legislature may make transfers of granted land that breached a transfer restriction void and provide for recovery of the land when the transferee’s title remained defeasible at the law’s commencement.
material_facts: The lands had been granted to members of disadvantaged communities subject to restrictions on transfer.
The purchasers acquired the lands in breach of those restrictions and were presumed to know of them.
Before the challenged law, such transfers were voidable and the land could be recovered through legal process.
The challenged law provided for recovery through an administrative process that included an opportunity for the affected person to be heard.
issues.conclusion: The legislature could make the still-defeasible transfers void and provide for their recovery; doing so did not unconstitutionally impair the transferees’ vested rights.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 4 and 5 of the Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prohibition of Transfer of Certain Lands) Act, 1978 could replace prolonged legal proceedings with a speedier process to protect the intended beneficiaries of the grants. A transferee who acquired land in breach of a known restriction acquired only a defeasible title, not a vested title immune from lawful avoidance. The measure furthered the State’s public policy of social and economic justice, consistent with Article 46 of the Constitution; the procedure must be consistent with natural justice.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_land_recovery_law and transfer_breached_grant_restriction and transferee_knew_of_restriction and title_still_defeasible_at_law_start and affected_person_given_hearing_opportunity

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_land_recover: The proceeding challenges the constitutionality of a law providing for recovery of land.
predicates.transfer_breached_grant_restriction: A transfer of granted land occurred in breach of a restriction governing that grant.
predicates.transferee_knew_of_restriction: The transferee knew, or was treated as knowing, of the restriction on transfer.
predicates.title_still_defeasible_at_law_start: The transferee’s title remained liable to be defeated when the recovery law commenced.
predicates.affected_person_given_hearing_opportunit: The recovery process gave the affected person an opportunity to be heard.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns recovery of granted land transferred in breach of a known restriction, and the transferee’s title remained defeasible and the affected person could be heard, the transfer may be made void and the land recovered.

issues.legal_issue: The recovery of granted land from a transferee with only a defeasible title, and the limited-period restriction imposed on the original grant, do not violate the constitutional right to acquire, hold and dispose of property.
material_facts: The original grants were made for the benefit and enjoyment of members of disadvantaged communities.
The grant terms restricted transfer for a specified period, rather than indefinitely.
The purchasers acquired the land in breach of the restriction and held only a defeasible title.
The purchasers challenged recovery without compensation under the constitutional property guarantee then in force.
issues.conclusion: The limited-period restriction was not unreasonable, and the recovery of land from transferees holding only defeasible titles did not violate Article 19(1)(f).
issues.legal_principle: Article 19(1)(f) did not invalidate the recovery measure. A limited transfer restriction was an essential condition of the grant, imposed to protect the grantee’s enjoyment of the land. A transferee who acquired only a defeasible right could not claim a constitutional violation when that right was defeated by lawful action; the Court also noted that transferees often enjoyed the land for a substantial period before its recovery.

rule.if: constitutional_property_right_challenge and land_granted_for_beneficiary_enjoyment and transfer_restriction_was_time_limited and transfer_breached_grant_restriction and transferee_had_only_defeasible_title

predicates.constitutional_property_right_challenge: The proceeding challenges land recovery under a constitutional guarantee of property rights.
predicates.land_granted_for_beneficiary_enjoyment: The land was granted for the benefit and enjoyment of its original recipient.
predicates.transfer_restriction_was_time_limited: The restriction on transferring the granted land applied for a specified period and was not perpetual.
predicates.transfer_breached_grant_restriction: A transfer of the granted land occurred in breach of the restriction governing the grant.
predicates.transferee_had_only_defeasible_title: The transferee’s title remained liable to be defeated under the law governing the grant.

issues.definition: If a property-rights challenge concerns a grant for the original recipient’s enjoyment, a time-limited transfer restriction, a transfer breaching that restriction, and a transferee with only defeasible title, recovery does not violate the property right.

issues.legal_issue: Recovery of land from a transferee whose interest is defeasible does not amount to deprivation or extinguishment of property protected by the constitutional provisions concerning property acquisition and agrarian reform.
material_facts: The purchasers acquired granted land in breach of restrictions and held defeasible interests.
The challenged law rendered the voidable transfers void and provided for recovery of the land.
The Court considered the nature of the transferees’ interests and held that they had no continuing property interest once the transfers were made void.
issues.conclusion: The law did not infringe Articles 31 or 31A because the transferees’ defeasible interests were not protected property of the kind those provisions addressed, and no acquisition or modification of their property rights arose.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on Amar Singh v. Custodian, Evacuee Property, Punjab, which held that an interest in land may not constitute property attracting constitutional property protections. Once a defeasible transfer is rendered void, the transferee has no remaining interest in the land; recovery of possession therefore does not amount to the State acquiring property from the transferee or modifying or extinguishing a protected property right. The Court considered Articles 31 and 31A of the Constitution.

predicates.constitutional_property_deprivation_chal: The proceeding challenges recovery as a constitutionally protected deprivation or alteration of property.
predicates.transferee_had_only_defeasible_title: The transferee’s interest in the land was liable to be defeated under the law governing the grant.
predicates.law_rendered_transfer_void_before_recove: The law made the transfer void before possession of the land was recovered.

issues.definition: When a deprivation challenge concerns recovery after a law has voided a transfer, and the transferee had only a defeasible title, recovery does not infringe the constitutional property-deprivation guarantees.

issues.legal_issue: A law that provides for recovery of granted land for the benefit of members of disadvantaged communities does not deny equal protection when that classification has a rational connection to protecting those communities’ economic interests.
material_facts: The law applied to land originally granted to members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
The stated purpose was to protect those communities’ economic interests and prevent their exploitation.
The Court regarded those communities as distinct and particularly vulnerable in the preservation of their economic interests.
issues.conclusion: The classification did not violate Article 14 because it had a clear nexus to the law’s protective purpose.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 permits special provisions for a distinct class when the classification has a rational nexus to the object sought to be achieved. The Court relied on the constitutional recognition of disadvantaged classes, including Articles 15(4) and 16(4), and the State’s duty under Article 46 to promote the interests of weaker sections, particularly Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, and protect them from exploitation.

predicates.equal_protection_challenge_to_targeted_l: The proceeding challenges the equal-protection validity of a law providing for recovery of granted land.
predicates.land_grants_targeted_to_distinct_disadva: The relevant land grants were made to a distinct disadvantaged class.
predicates.recovery_law_aimed_to_protect_class_econ: The recovery law was intended to protect that class’s economic interests and prevent exploitation.
predicates.classification_connected_to_protective_o: The class selected for the law’s special treatment was connected to its protective purpose.

issues.definition: If a land-recovery law challenged on equal-protection grounds targets grants to a distinct disadvantaged class to protect that class’s economic interests, the classification is valid when connected to that purpose.

issues.legal_issue: The recovery law does not apply to a transfer made after a transfer restriction expired, to a transfer that did not breach the applicable restriction, or to a transferee whose title had become perfected before the law commenced.
material_facts: The law applied to transfers made in breach of restrictions governing granted land.
Some transfers could have occurred after the restriction had expired or without breaching a restriction.
A transferee could initially have acquired a defeasible title but perfected it through prescription before the law commenced.
The Court held that the law could not render void a title that was no longer defeasible when the law commenced.
issues.conclusion: The law had to be read down so that it applied only where the transfer breached the restriction and the transferee’s title remained defeasible at the law’s commencement.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 4 and 5 apply to transfers made in breach of a condition restricting transfer. A title perfected by prescription before commencement is no longer defeasible and cannot be rendered void by the law without violating the constitutional guarantee. The Court therefore construed section 4 not to affect titles that were not voidable at commencement.

rule.if: land_grant_transfer_recovery_proceeding and (transfer_after_restriction_expired or transfer_did_not_breach_restriction or title_perfected_before_law_start)

predicates.land_grant_transfer_recovery_proceeding: The proceeding concerns recovery of land originally granted subject to a transfer restriction.
predicates.transfer_after_restriction_expired: The granted land was transferred after the applicable transfer restriction had expired.
predicates.transfer_did_not_breach_restriction: The transfer did not contravene the restriction governing the grant.
predicates.title_perfected_before_law_start: The transferee’s title had become perfected before the recovery law commenced.

issues.definition: In a proceeding to recover granted land, a transfer is outside the recovery law if the restriction had expired, the transfer did not breach the restriction, or the transferee’s title had been perfected before the law commenced.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge to the absence of an appeal in the original recovery law requires no further constitutional ruling once an appeal provision has been enacted during the case.
material_facts: The original law provided no appeal from the relevant administrative order.
During the case, an amendment added an appeal provision.
The Court consequently did not make a final pronouncement on whether the original absence of an appeal made the law constitutionally unreasonable.
issues.conclusion: The question did not survive for further consideration after the amendment provided an appeal, and the Court made no final ruling on the original appeal provision’s constitutionality.
issues.legal_principle: The Court expressed doubt that the absence of an appeal might constitute procedural unreasonableness, but did not decide that issue because an amendment supplied an appeal against the administrative order before judgment.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_no_appeal: The proceeding challenges the constitutionality of a recovery process that originally provided no appeal.
predicates.appeal_added_before_final_decision: An appeal provision was added to the recovery process before the court made its final decision.

issues.definition: When an appeal is added before final decision in a case challenging the original absence of an appeal, no further constitutional ruling on that challenge is necessary.

issues.legal_issue: A delay in appealing an administrative recovery order may be condoned where the appeal is filed within the transitional period after a new appeal right takes effect, if the appeal is otherwise maintainable and justice supports entertaining it.
material_facts: An amendment newly provided an appeal against an administrative recovery order.
The amendment prescribed a period for filing an appeal from the order, although the appeal right had not existed when earlier orders were made.

The Court stated that the appellate authority could consider condoning delay where an appeal was filed within three months after the new appeal right came into force, subject to maintainability and the interests of justice.
issues.conclusion: The appellate authority may condone the delay in such a transitional appeal if it is otherwise maintainable and the interests of justice require that it be heard.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the condonation power under section 5 of the Limitation Act, as made available to the appellate authority under section 5A of the amended recovery law. It indicated that the newly created appeal right and the prescribed filing period could justify condoning delay for an appeal filed within the stated transitional period, provided the authority was satisfied that the appeal was otherwise maintainable and justice required its admission.

rule.if: appeal_from_administrative_recovery_order and appeal_right_newly_created and appeal_filed_within_transition_period and appeal_otherwise_maintainable and interests_of_justice_favor_hearing

predicates.appeal_from_administrative_recovery_orde: The proceeding is an appeal from an administrative order recovering granted land.
predicates.appeal_right_newly_created: The right of appeal became available only after the administrative order was made.
predicates.appeal_filed_within_transition_period: The appeal was filed within the transitional period following the new appeal right’s commencement.
predicates.appeal_otherwise_maintainable: The appeal satisfies the requirements for being entertained apart from the question of delay.
predicates.interests_of_justice_favor_hearing: The appellate authority considers that the interests of justice favor hearing the appeal.

issues.definition: A delay in an appeal from an administrative recovery order may be condoned when the appeal right was newly created, the appeal was filed within the transitional period, the appeal is otherwise maintainable, and the interests of justice favor hearing it.
